subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit Docker sandbox recovery path for hosts where `--security-opt no-new-privileges` prevents even `/usr/bin/sleep` from execing?
rationale: The bug is well isolated, but disabling or bypassing `no-new-privileges` changes the Docker sandbox security boundary and repository policy favors explicit operator-controlled tradeoffs over silent compatibility fallback.

options.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
options.body: Keep the secure default and add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, documentation, focused tests, and real host proof.

options.title: Diagnostic-only recovery
options.body: Keep the hardening unconditional and improve startup/session/doctor errors so affected hosts get a precise explanation and supported mitigation guidance without weakening the sandbox.

options.title: Declare host combo unsupported
options.body: Document that Docker hosts rejecting `no-new-privileges` are unsupported for Docker sandbox mode and direct users to another sandbox backend or host configuration.

recommendation.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the secure default and add a clearly named `sandbox.docker` opt-out with dangerous-config reporting, documentation, focused tests, and real host proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest history on the existing hardening flag and dangerous Docker override policy that this decision would extend.
